conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of your hospital doctors. You were brought in with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, thank you. Five days ago, I started having that familiar squeezing pain in my upper belly, like before. It goes into my back. I’ve been nauseous, throwing up, and couldn’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds like your usual pancreatitis flare. You mentioned this feels like your typical pain. Any fever, chills, or chest pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever or chest pain. I did have loose stools for a couple days, but that’s stopped now. I haven’t had a bowel movement in two days though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Your labs came back mostly normal. Your lipase is 43, which is only slightly elevated. But given your history, we’re treating this as a flare of chronic pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I’ve had so many of these. I just couldn’t handle the dry heaves anymore, even with my Phenergan shot at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve started you on IV fluids to rehydrate you. For pain, we’re giving Toradol and Dilaudid, and for nausea, Promethazine and Ativan, just like your usual protocol.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good, thank you. My blood pressure was high in the ER—was that from the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was 180/110. That’s likely due to pain, anxiety, and maybe missing your blood pressure meds. We’ve restarted your lisinopril and amlodipine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on those for a while. My last check was high, so I’m not surprised.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep an eye on it. Also, your blood cultures were negative—no infection. And your tox screen showed amitriptyline and tramadol, which are on your list, so that’s expected.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I take amitriptyline at night for sleep and depression. And tramadol as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing all your home meds, including seroquel, omeprazole, and Creon. We switched omeprazole to IV pantoprazole for now since you can’t take pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s fine. I know the drill. How long do you think I’ll be here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you until your pain is controlled and you can eat without vomiting. That usually takes a few days with your condition.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still there, but a bit better. I’m not dry heaving as much. Can I try a little water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start you on clear liquids slowly. If you keep that down, we can advance your diet tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m so tired of IV fluids. My mouth feels dry even with them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s common. We’re also watching your electrolytes. Your bicarbonate was a bit low yesterday, but it’s improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well overnight—no vomiting. We’re upgrading you to a soft diet. How’s the pain now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. Still tender, but I can handle it. Can I switch back to my oral pain meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start your tramadol by mouth. We’ll taper the IV pain meds as you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Creon? I need that with food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Already ordered. One capsule with each meal and snack. We’ll keep that up when you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What about my blood pressure? It’s still high this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s around 150s/90s. We’re going to increase your amlodipine from 5mg to 10mg daily before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll need to check it at home. My partner can help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. You’ve kept down solid food for two meals. Pain is mild. We’re planning for discharge in the next day or two.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. Will I go home with the same meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your home medications. We’re switching back to oral omeprazole and stopping the IV pantoprazole.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the amlodipine increase—that’s permanent?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: For now. Your primary doctor will follow up and adjust as needed. Make sure to monitor your BP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Any tests to explain why these flares are happening more often?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your CT and MRCP in the past were normal. You mentioned your parents are CFTR carriers—that might be a factor. But we don’t have a clear cause yet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve wondered if that’s why I have chronic pancreatitis. No alcohol, had my gallbladder out—so that’s the only thing that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’ll note that for your outpatient team to consider further testing if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge tomorrow. You’ve been off IV meds for a day, eating regular food, and pain is minimal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Will I need another midline like last time? My veins are tough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, you don’t need one this time. You’re back on oral meds and eating, so we won’t need long-term IV access.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I hate those. What about my mood? I’ve been okay, but depression still weighs on me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve stayed at your baseline. We continued seroquel and amitriptyline. Keep in touch with your mental health provider.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And headaches—I’ve had one, used Fioricet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. Continue as needed. Just don’t overuse it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final check before discharge. Your labs today are stable. Hemoglobin is a bit low but not new. Blood pressure is better on the higher amlodipine dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel ready to go home. Just want to rest in my own bed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get discharge instructions and a med list. Make sure to follow up with your primary doctor in a week for BP check.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll schedule that today. Thank you for helping me through this flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call if symptoms return or worsen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your discharge papers are ready. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m glad this one wasn’t as bad as some.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You responded well to the protocol. Keep taking your meds, eat small meals, and monitor your blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. And I’ll call my doctor this week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll send the records to your team. Take care, and we hope to see you only for routine visits from now on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s the goal. Thanks again.
